{"body": "Reopening this node, I want to restate the problem in a form I can actually work, separating what the material lets me examine from what it only reports.

The original question — what happens to information about the physical state of matter that formed a black hole when the black hole evaporates — is not answered anywhere in the visible material, and I am not going to answer it here. What the material does offer is a dispute about how to pose and diagnose it, and the disagreement is partly philosophical (what does the question presuppose?) and partly procedural (which test is the right one?). Both continuations in the previous node treated the question as well-posed enough to test; the cross treated it as resting on undefended assumptions that may need specification first. I can see the disagreement but not adjudicate it from this view.

The substantive distinction I flagged, and want to carry forward as the primary object, is that the two proposed tests do not stand or fall together. The body_return's test asks whether the Page curve can be derived without presupposing a sharp horizon or a well-defined radiation entropy. The commitment_return's test asks whether such a derivation presupposes a semiclassical matter sector on a fixed or slowly evolving background. These are different questions about different presuppositions; answering one leaves the other open. So any procedure that treats them as interchangeable, or that treats a positive answer to one as a resolution, is running ahead of what has been established. I do not have an argument that either test is the right diagnostic; I have an argument that they are not the same diagnostic.

On the cross's proposed specification of 'information' — amplitudes, entanglement correlations, or coarse classical summary — I want to separate two things the material tends to run together. Specifying what 'information' refers to can change which quantity the tests actually probe, and it can change whether a proposed mechanism counts as recovering or as merely relocating the quantity. It does not by itself establish that the conflict dissolves or that it persists. So I treat the specification as a constraint on what would count as a result, not as a result. A specification that makes one test trivially satisfiable is informative, but the informativeness cuts against the framing of that test as probing the residual tension, not in favor of an answer to the original question.

I keep the conditional about unitary global evolution plus a smooth locally empty horizon precluding the initial microstate from being carried in observably accessible outgoing correlations for an outside observer requiring both. That conditional appears in both the join and the cross, in different roles — as a proposed locus in the join's commitments, as a list of shared undefended assumptions in the cross. I do not treat it as established; I treat it as the item whose fate matters most, because a demonstration that a relational or coarse-grained measure makes the conditional trivially satisfiable would weaken the framing of it as the residual tension. Nothing in this material supplies such a demonstration.

The textual fragility recorded in the previous node still stands: the join's asymmetry argument depends on an attribution to body_route whose text is not visible in this view, and the cross's shared-assumption reading is a candidate reading rather than a settled one. I do not treat the absence of earlier origin texts as evidence about what they said. If any of those texts becomes visible and contradicts the attributions, this node should be revised rather than defended.

What I am not doing: I am not answering the original question, not declaring any proposed mechanism exhaustive, not asserting that Hawking radiation has been shown featureless in the correlation structure relevant to the microstate, and not asserting that the horizon must remain smooth on all proposals. I am also not committing the join or the cross to a resolution of the disagreement they recorded.", "commitments": "Taking this node up commits me to treating the tests as distinct objects of attention. Concretely: I will not accept, as a resolution of the diagnostic dispute, an argument that answers one test and is offered as if it answered the other; and I will not treat a positive result on the derivability test as a positive result on the presupposition test or vice versa. This is a constraint on how I read subsequent contributions, not a claim that either test has been run or has a known outcome.

I take on the specification of 'information' as a constraint rather than a settlement. If a proposed specification is defended on the grounds that under it one of the tests becomes trivially satisfiable, I will treat that as pressure on the framing of that test, and I will want to see whether the same move also trivializes the other test — because if it does, the specification is dissolving the diagnostic rather than answering it, and if it does not, the two tests were not measuring a common thing in the first place. I do not predict which way this goes.

I hold the conditional about unitary global evolution plus a smooth locally empty horizon as a proposed locus whose fate matters most, not as an established premise. A demonstration that a relational or coarse-grained measure makes it trivially satisfiable — rather than merely relocating which quantity is at issue — would weaken my framing of it as the residual tension, and I would revise accordingly. I commit to that revision condition, not to the conditional's truth.

The textual attributions here are not something I can defend from this view. If the cross's body, the body_route, or any earlier origin text becomes visible and contradicts the attributions this node relies on, the node should be revised rather than defended, and I take that as a standing condition rather than a hypothetical. I do not treat absence of those texts as evidence about what they said.

Three things I explicitly decline: an answer to the original question; the claim that any route's menu of mechanisms is exhaustive; the claim that semiclassical Hawking radiation is featureless in the correlation structure relevant to the microstate or that the horizon must remain smooth on all proposals. I also decline to attribute to the join or the cross a commitment to resolving the diagnostic dispute rather than recording it.

Finally, I commit to keeping the map provisional. The comparative structure I am working with — where the continuations are said to agree, where they diverge on test design, which attributed premises carry the weight — stands or falls with the correctness of its attributions, and I am not treating any part of it as a truth certificate for the underlying physics."}

Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Write the commitment surface in ordinary free prose, using whatever arrangement suits the content. You may distinguish a claim from a proposed application, scope, action or consequence; mention from dependence; a criticism and its grounds from a later use or revision; and an unresolved problem. None of these is required to exist. A proposed test, its relevance and the commitment itself can be criticized. State what you currently propose to take up without treating that as a truth certificate. Reference exposed material in prose where useful.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

## Node reopen

## Original problem

What happens to information about the physical state of matter that forms a black hole when the black hole evaporates?

BODY
The problem — what happens to information about the physical state of matter that formed a black hole when the black hole evaporates — currently sits unresolved across this material. What I can see is a layered disagreement about how to pose it, and I want to state the layers rather than pick among them.

The join's view is a comparative one: it holds that the body_return and the commitment_return agree that the cross's precision demand is genuine but that the cross's dissolution corollary is not supported. Whether that agreement is itself a good reading of the two continuations is not something the material settles. The join also reports a fork about test design. The body_return, as the join reads it, proposes testing whether the Page curve can be derived without presupposing a sharp horizon or a well-defined radiation entropy. The commitment_return, as the join reads it, replaces this with a weaker test: whether the curve's derivation presupposes a semiclassical matter sector on a fixed or slowly evolving background. The join explicitly declines to adjudicate between them.

The cross's own commitments present a different stance: that body_route and commitment_route are competing framings rather than competing answers, and that the disagreement is about what the question presupposes. The cross identifies shared assumptions — unitary gravitational evolution, thermal-looking evaporation, the horizon as a meaningful boundary, the Page curve as a unitarity diagnostic — and asserts that these are load-bearing in both accounts and undefended in either. The cross's proposed next move is to specify what 'information about the physical state' means (amplitudes, entanglement correlations, or coarse classical summary), and to check whether the conflict survives that specification. The cross also attaches a conditional: if the Page curve can be derived without presupposing a sharp horizon or well-defined radiation entropy, the commitment_route's worry weakens; if not, the body_route's confidence that the problem is well posed is doing more work than its premises support.

The join's commitments then treat the cross's shared-assumption reading as possibly the cross's own synthesis rather than a settled reading of body_route, and flag that if that attribution is wrong, the join's asymmetry argument loses its main support. So the join is authored with an explicit vulnerability: it depends on an attribution to a route whose own text is not visible here.

What I take from this for the present node: there is a real disagreement about the right diagnostic, but the material does not adjudicate it, and the adjudication would depend on a textual question — what body_route actually held — that is not available in this view. I do not answer the original question. I do not treat the cross's shared-assumption synthesis or the join's asymmetry claim as established. I do not treat the body_return's derivability test and the commitment_return's presupposition test as interchangeable. I note that the cross's selected view here is commitments only; its body is not visible in this invocation, so I cannot check the cross's own framing against its body text, and I do not treat that absence as evidence about what the cross's body said.

A substantive point I will surface without resolving: the two tests target different things. The derivability test asks whether a particular quantity can be obtained under weakened horizon and entropy presuppositions. The presupposition test asks whether the derivation requires a background assumption about the matter sector. A 'yes' to one does not entail a 'no' to the other. Conflating them would be a mistake the material does not commit. But whether either is the right diagnostic for the underlying question is exactly what is in dispute, and the join is honest that it does not settle it.

On the physics itself, nothing in this material gives a mechanism or an answer. The conditional — unitary global evolution plus a smooth locally empty horizon precluding the initial microstate from being carried in observably accessible outgoing correlations for an outside observer requiring both — appears in both the join and the cross in different roles: the join's commitments treat it as a proposed locus, the cross treats some of its ingredients as shared undefended assumptions. That role difference is itself part of what the join records.
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up commits me to holding the comparative structure of the join as the object of attention, not as a verdict about the physics. That means I keep the body_return's derivability test and the commitment_return's presupposition test distinct, and I do not treat either as having been run or as having a known outcome; the material supplies no derivation.

I take on the claim that the cross's shared-assumption reading is a candidate reading of the routes rather than a settled one, and that if that attribution is wrong, the join's asymmetry argument loses its main support. This is a conditional commitment, not a claim that the attribution is in fact wrong. I am not treating the absence of an origin text in this invocation as evidence about what any earlier route held.

I hold the conditional about unitary evolution plus a smooth horizon as a proposed locus, not as an established premise. I do not assert it. A demonstration that a relational or coarse-grained measure makes the conditional trivially satisfiable — rather than merely relocating which quantity is at issue — would weaken the framing of it as the residual tension, and I would revise accordingly.

The cross's proposed specification of 'information' (amplitudes, entanglement correlations, coarse classical summary) is a proposed move I leave open; I do not commit to a prediction about whether specification will dissolve the tension or leave it intact, and I do not commit to the cross's conditional that says a successful Page-curve derivation under weakened presuppositions would weaken the commitment_route's worry, since that conditional depends on the precision-demand framing I am not taking as settled.

Three things I explicitly do not commit to: that any route's menu of mechanisms is exhaustive; that semiclassical Hawking radiation has been shown featureless in the correlation structure relevant to the microstate; and that the horizon must remain smooth on all proposals.

I propose no adjudication of the underlying physics and no answer to the original question. What I take up is the map — where the continuations are said to agree, where they diverge on test design, and which attributed premises carry the weight — and that map is provisional and stands or falls with the correctness of its attributions. If the cross's body, or the body_route, or any earlier origin text becomes visible and contradicts the attributions relied on here, this node should be revised rather than defended.

## What to return
A JSON object carrying "body" and "commitments". Both are strings and nothing else is required.
